## PM claim + dispatch order — R18

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6160-merge-group-floor-derived`.

### Ruling: **option 2** — derive the floor from `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`. ⛔ Not option 1.

The card frames this as cheap-but-open (add two entries) versus more-coverage-but-denser (cross-check the two declarations). Taking option 2, and the reason is not "more coverage" — it is that **option 1 leaves the same hole for workflow nine, and PR #6159 already demonstrated the failure mode by adding its own entry by hand without closing the class.** A hand-maintained floor that has already fallen behind twice will fall behind a third time.

**The objection I had to answer first**, because it is the strongest one: the map's own header says the floor *cannot* be derived, since *"may this context be required?"* is a property of repository settings and not of the YAML. That is correct — and option 2 does not violate it. `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` in `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` is **already a human declaration of exactly that property**, written down elsewhere in this repo. Deriving from it is not mechanising an unmechanisable judgement; it is stopping the same judgement from being written down twice and drifting. That is the same principle this lane applied on #6138 and #6152: remove the second source of truth rather than build machinery to keep it honest.

The hand-maintained map keeps carrying the **reasons**. It stops carrying the membership.

### ⚠️ The condition that decides whether this is sound — measure it, do not assume it

Deriving a floor from `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` is a strict improvement **only if `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` is a superset of what the map names today**. The card's table implies it (8 unfiltered blocking checks vs 6 named workflows), but implied is not measured.

**Measure the containment in both directions before you write the assertion**, and state both readings:

- Every workflow named in `MUST_SUBSCRIBE_MERGE_GROUP` also produces a `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` check → the derivation loses nothing.
- Every workflow producing a `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` check is on `main` and subscribes `merge_group` → the derived floor is satisfiable today.

⛔ **If the first direction fails for even one workflow, stop and hand back.** A derived floor that silently *narrows* is worse than the hand-maintained one it replaced: it would look like more coverage while asserting less. That is the exact shape this card exists to catch, one level up, and shipping it would be an own goal.

**Pin the containment itself**, so the two declarations cannot cross later without something going red. A derivation with no pin on its own precondition is the next hand-maintained floor.

### Non-vacuity — the part I will check hardest

`dependabot-merge-gate.test.ts` already maps check names back to the workflow files that produce them; reuse that mapping rather than writing a second one.

Prove the new assertion can fail, with mutation shown on disk and restore verified:

1. Delete the `merge_group:` trigger from `doc-component-types.yml` → the new assertion **must** red. Today nothing anywhere notices; that is the whole card. This is the positive control and it is **not optional** — an assertion that stays green under the defect it was written for is not an assertion.
2. Delete it from `docs-links.yml` → the **existing** test must still red, proving you did not replace working coverage with weaker coverage.
3. Add a synthetic `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` entry naming a workflow that does not subscribe → the derived floor must red, i.e. it tracks the other declaration rather than a snapshot of it.

Restore with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` (never the bare form), and prove restoration with an empty `git diff HEAD`.

### Scope

`scripts/__tests__/merge-queue-reporting.test.ts` and whatever minimal read of `dependabot-merge-gate.mjs`'s declaration the derivation needs. ⛔ Do not edit any workflow YAML — nothing is broken on disk today; both doc gates really do subscribe, and the deliverable is the missing assertion, not a fix.

Context worth keeping in view: the map exists because a required context that does not report on a queue build does not fail the queue, it **stalls** it to the ruleset's 60-minute timeout (#3523, which cost #3503 / #3510 / #3516 merging with `Type Check` at `conclusion=failure`). Cite that in the test's header so the next reader knows what the floor is protecting.

## ⚠️ Correction to my dispatch order above — one line was truncated by GitHub's sanitizer

The restore instruction in the **Non-vacuity** section was posted as:

> Restore with `git checkout HEAD -- ` (never the bare form), and prove restoration with an empty `git diff HEAD`.

That is **not** what I wrote. The angle-bracket fragment naming the path was eaten on write, so the order now displays the bare form immediately before telling you never to use the bare form. ⛔ Read it as:

> Restore with **`git checkout HEAD -- ` followed by the explicit path** — never the bare two-dash form with no path after it.

Nothing else in the order changed, and no ruling is affected. The three ablations, the containment precondition, and the ⛔ hand-back condition all stand exactly as written.

⭐ Recording how this was caught, because it is the same lesson the order itself is about: the dev on #6179 hit the sanitizer eating its report marker, said so, and re-posted. Reading **their** note is what made me read **my own** comment back — which I had not done, despite instructing every dev in this lane to do exactly that. Two of this round's five orders were damaged; #5940's, #5867's and #6172's are intact. Filed as a process defect in objectstack rather than left as a one-off fix here.

## PM review — ACCEPTED. PR #6187 armed (ready + auto-merge SQUASH).

Reviewed against the branch. I re-derived the containment measurement independently rather than reading it back, because the whole ruling rests on it.

### ⭐ The card's premise had GROWN while it sat — and that settles the option-1-vs-2 argument by itself

The card measured **6 named** against **8 unfiltered blocking checks**. Re-measured on `b37d3f0fd`: **7 named** against **10 workflows producing a `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` check**.

Both numbers moved, in the direction the card predicted:

- `pre-install-import-graph.yml` joined the map — added **by hand** by PR #6159, which is the route-1 behaviour the card called out.
- `doc-fence-languages.yml` joined the *producers* and **not** the map — so the hand-maintained list fell behind a **third** time, in the hours between the card being filed and being worked.

I had ruled option 2 on the argument that "a floor that has already fallen behind twice will fall behind a third time." It fell behind a third time **during the round**. That is the ruling confirmed by the tree rather than by me.

### My own measurement, both directions

I parsed `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` and every workflow on `main` myself:

| direction | reading |
| --- | --- |
| workflows producing a `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` check | **10** |
| …of those, subscribing `merge_group` on `main` | **10 — zero violations** |
| `MUST_SUBSCRIBE_MERGE_GROUP` named entries | **7** |
| …of those, inside the producing set | **7 — zero violations** |
| derivation | **widens 7 → 10** |

⚠️ My first parse returned **0 named**, because the map is a `new Map([...])` and I read it as an object literal. Zero on one leg with a nonzero other leg is a broken instrument, not a finding — I refused it and reparsed rather than reporting "0 → 10". Second time tonight that the same class of parser error nearly produced a confident wrong number in a review.

**Direction 1 holding is what makes this safe to land.** The ⛔ hand-back condition was a derived floor that silently *narrows*; it does not narrow, it strictly widens, and it widens onto three workflows that all already subscribe — so no YAML change was needed and none was made. Confirmed: **zero files under `.github/workflows/` in the diff.**

### The pins, including one I did not ask for

All three required assertions exist:

- `loses nothing the hand-maintained map named` — the **containment precondition, pinned**, so the two declarations cannot cross later without going red. This was the non-negotiable one.
- `requires merge_group of every workflow that produces a required context` — the derived floor itself.
- ⭐ `resolves every required context to the workflow that produces it` — **not in my order.** It catches a *renamed* check that resolves to no workflow, which would silently shrink the floor while every other assertion stayed green. Alongside it is a guard that the derivation did not produce *nothing* ("Either `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` was emptied or `producedCheckNames()` stopped working"). That is an anti-vacuity pin on the derivation's own output — the same discipline that just saved me from my 0-named parse, written into the test.

The three ablations all ran with direction predicted first, mutation proven on disk by anchored grep rather than an editor exit code, a trap on EXIT/INT/TERM, and restore by `git checkout HEAD --` plus the explicit path proven with an empty `git diff HEAD`. ⭐ **A1 is the positive control and it discriminates**: deleting `merge_group` from `doc-component-types.yml` reds the **new** assertion while the **existing** map assertion stays green — because that file is not in the map. That is precisely the defect this card was filed for, previously invisible, now caught. A2 confirms the old coverage was not replaced by weaker coverage.

⭐ And the stale-artifact leg was **closed rather than skipped**: the assertions read `.github/workflows` from disk and import `dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` by relative **source** path, so nothing resolves through a `dist` and there is no false-green to defeat. Saying *why* there is no rebuild leg is better than silently not having one.

### The one thing that went beyond my stated scope, and why I am accepting it

My order scoped this to the test file plus a minimal read of `dependabot-merge-gate.mjs`. The diff also touches `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` (26 lines). I read it before deciding, and it is **consequential, not creep** — the page said, in as many words:

> …nothing derives the set, because "may this context be required?" is a property of the repository's settings, which no test here can read.

This PR makes that **false**. Shipping it unchanged would have left a newly-false claim in a docs page, which is the exact class this lane has carded three times tonight (#6086, #6164, #6179). ⭐ And the replacement keeps the half that is still true — *"'May this context be required?' is still a property of the repository's settings that no test here can read — `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` is a human's answer to it"* — which is my ruling's own reasoning, restated for a docs reader rather than parroted.

The authoring instruction beside it was updated to match (name the context in `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`, and the workflow is inside the floor from that moment), and the #4154 doc-enumeration scan now runs over the **union** of the map and the derived floor — without which the page could freely enumerate the three subscribers the map had fallen behind by. That second consequence is subtle and was caught unprompted.

### One parser, not two

The check-name→workflow-file mapping moved into `scripts/__tests__/workflow-checks.ts` and is imported by both test files, as ordered. ⚠️ Worth recording the reason it is a **module** rather than an export of the test file: importing a test file from another test file **re-registers its `describe` blocks in the importer**. That is a real trap and the note will save someone a confusing duplicate-suite failure.

### CI and landing

16 checks green, 0 failures, 6 running (4 shards, Type Check, Lint — normal contention). Auto-merge fires only on all-green, so arming does not bypass anything. No changeset owed — the presence gate's own verdict says so.

The two 15-second timeouts in the full `scripts/` run were correctly diagnosed rather than waved off: both build real git fixture repos, both pass in isolation, and neither file is touched by this diff nor reads anything it changes.
